PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS
Infective exacerbation of COPD (J44.1) with acute hypercapnic (type 2) respiratory failure - resolved.

CO-MORBIDITIES
COPD GOLD 3 (FEV1 41% predicted, 2025); type 2 diabetes on metformin; hypertension; osteoarthritis both knees. Ex-smoker, 35 pack-years, stopped 2016.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT
4/7 of increasing breathlessness, purulent sputum and new confusion; brought in by her daughter. On arrival RR 28, SpO2 81% on air, NEWS2 7. ABG (on 2 L): pH 7.29, pCO2 8.4 kPa, pO2 7.1 kPa, HCO3 30.

COURSE IN HOSPITAL
Started on NIV (IPAP 20 / EPAP 5) on AMU and weaned over 36 h; transferred to Seacole Ward 05/10. CXR: hyperinflation, no consolidation. Sputum grew Haemophilus influenzae (doxycycline-sensitive); penicillin allergy, so treated with oral doxycycline. Prednisolone 30 mg OD for 5 days, completed 08/10. Reviewed by the COPD nurse specialist, ⟦name|Bernadette McAllister⟧, who checked inhaler technique, switched her to a single triple-therapy inhaler and issued a new rescue pack with a written plan. ⟦name|Folasade⟧ walked 40 m with the physio on 08/10 with SpO2 89-92% on air (target 88-92%) and was keen to go home. Capillary glucose up to 16.4 mmol/L on steroids; metformin was held because of an AKI (creatinine peak 142, now 97).

MEDICATION ON DISCHARGE
Trelegy Ellipta 92/55/22 micrograms   1 puff once daily        NEW - replaces Fostair 100/6
Salbutamol 100 micrograms MDI         2 puffs PRN via spacer    unchanged
Doxycycline 100 mg                    once daily                2 more days, last dose 11/10/2026
Amlodipine 5 mg                       once daily                unchanged
Metformin 500 mg                      twice daily               WITHHELD - see GP actions
Rescue pack: doxycycline 200 mg stat then 100 mg OD x 5 days + prednisolone 30 mg OD x 5 days

ALLERGIES / ADRs
Penicillin - widespread rash (1994)

ACTIONS FOR GP
1. U&E in 1 week; if eGFR > 45 please restart metformin.
2. Recheck BP (150s systolic on the ward, possibly steroid-related).
3. Please confirm pulmonary rehab referral has been received (ref PR-26-0918, Bolton Community Respiratory Team).

FOLLOW-UP
Respiratory clinic with Dr ⟦name|Pryce-Jenkins⟧ in approx. 6 weeks - appointment letter to follow.

NEXT OF KIN / CARER
Ms ⟦name|Kemi Adeyemi-Clarke⟧ (daughter; LPA health & welfare registered 2023) - mobile ⟦phone number|07700 900662⟧. ⟦name|Folasade⟧ is happy for ⟦name|Kemi⟧ to be given information about her care.

INFORMATION GIVEN
Discharge plan discussed with patient and daughter. "Living with COPD" booklet (Asthma + Lung UK) given. Patient knows to call 999 if severely breathless or drowsy.

– V. a. stenosierende KHK (I25.19), CCS-Klasse II
– Arterielle Hypertonie, unzureichend eingestellt (I10.90)
– Hypercholesterinämie (E78.0), LDL-C 168 mg/dl

Anamnese

Familienanamnese positiv: Bruder ⟦name|Rainer⟧ (63 J.) erlitt 2022 einen Vorderwandinfarkt. Herr ⟦name|Schimanski⟧ arbeitet als Lokführer bei der Regiobahn und ist begeisterter Hobbyradfahrer (nach eigener Aussage „seit Jan Ullrich 1997 jedes Wochenende auf dem Rad").

Befunde

Ruhe-EKG: Sinusrhythmus, Linkstyp, keine Erregungsrückbildungsstörungen.
TTE: LVEF ca. 58 % (biplan nach Simpson), keine regionalen Wandbewegungsstörungen, Aortenklappe trikuspide, keine relevanten Vitien.
Ergometrie: Belastung bis 125 W (73 % der Soll-Leistung), Abbruch wegen typischer AP; deszendierende ST-Senkung 1,5 mm in V4–V6, Rückbildung nach 4 Min.
Labor (12.10.2026): hs-Troponin T 9 ng/l, Kreatinin 0,94 mg/dl, HbA1c 5,8 %, Kalium 4,3 mmol/l.

Beurteilung und Procedere
Bei typischer Angina pectoris und positiver Ergometrie besteht eine hohe Vortestwahrscheinlichkeit für eine KHK. Wir haben für den 28.10.2026 eine Koronarangiographie im Evangelischen Krankenhaus Kaiserswerth angemeldet (Aufnahme Station K3, 07:30 Uhr, nüchtern). Die Ehefrau, Frau ⟦name|Birgit Schimanski-Lindqvist⟧, begleitet ihn; sie ist tagsüber unter ⟦phone number|02102 87 31 14⟧ erreichbar und bittet nach dem Eingriff um Rückruf.
